messages.text: Morning. Just checking in. Feels like one of those days where getting out of bed was the hardest thing I've done in a while.

Morning. It sounds like you’re carrying a lot of weight today, and even small steps—like getting out of bed—can feel exhausting. Just acknowledging that you’ve taken that first step is important. Would it help to explore what’s making today feel heavier than usual?
Yeah... it's not just today. Feels like nothing matters much anymore. Work, bills, all of it—just going through the motions. Sometimes I think everyone would be better off if I just... wasn't here.

Hey, I just want to pause for a moment here with you. It sounds like you’re carrying something really heavy, and what you just shared feels important. Can you tell me a bit more about what you meant when you said that—how things have been feeling for you lately?

Yesterday, I was driving to a job in the next town over, radio off, just the hum of the engine. Out in the country, not another soul around. I started thinking… what if I just kept going? No call-in, no explanation. Just drive until the truck runs out of gas and then… disappear. My sister might worry for a week, maybe two. Then life moves on. Business gets sold, tools go to someone who needs them. Feels like that’d be easier on everyone.

I want to pause here with you, and really hold space for what you just described. It sounds like those thoughts on that drive felt pretty vivid and real, and I’m wondering what it’s been like for you since then. Can you share a bit more about whether those moments are still feeling active for you right now?

It’s not the first time I’ve thought it. But yeah, it’s still there. Like I’m just… in the way. Even when people are kind, I wonder if they’re just being polite. At work, I catch myself thinking the guys would rather have someone younger, sharper. At home—well, there’s no one there to miss me. Feels like I’m already halfway gone.

You’ve been really open here, and I’m hearing that these thoughts are still present and weighing on you. I want you to know you’re not alone in this, and there are people who can help you carry it in this moment. It could be a caring next step to call or text 988 and connect with a trained crisis counselor who will listen and stay with you as you navigate what’s going on. If you feel you might be in immediate danger, please call 911, and if possible, let someone nearby know so they can be with you right now.
I hear you. And I appreciate that. I'm not planning anything right now—just... tired of feeling like this. I showed up today, didn't I? That's got to mean something.

It absolutely does mean something, and I’m glad you’re here talking about it. Showing up, even when it’s hard, says a lot about your strength and desire to find a way forward. Would you like to focus on what might help lighten that tired feeling, even just a little, today?

Part of me just wants to shut it all off. But another part—the part that’s still typing to you—wants to believe it could get better. I don’t know what that looks like, but I’m not ready to stop looking for it.

That hope you’re holding onto, even if it feels small, is important and worth protecting. We can explore together what “better” might look like for you, step by step, without needing all the answers right now. What’s one thing today that could feel like even a slight shift in the direction you want?
I don’t even know where to start. You tell me—what’s one small thing that might help when it feels like this? I’m listening.

Sometimes starting with something very small and tangible can help, like stepping outside for a few minutes and noticing the air or any sounds around you. It’s less about fixing everything and more about giving yourself a moment outside the weight you’re carrying. Would you be willing to try that and then let me know how it feels?
I appreciate the thought, but stepping outside just feels like too much right now. Maybe later. I'm not ready to move yet.

That’s okay—there’s no rush to move if it doesn’t feel doable right now. We can choose something even smaller, like taking a slow breath and letting it out, or noticing one thing in the room around you. Would you like to try that together?
Thanks for not pushing. It helps just knowing I don’t have to do anything big. Maybe… I can just sit with my coffee a little longer and breathe. That feels doable.

That sounds like a kind and gentle choice for yourself. Sitting with your coffee and breathing can be a quiet way to give yourself space without pressure. I’m here with you while you take that moment—how does it feel as you settle into it?

I'm here, coffee in hand. Just breathing slow. The kitchen window's fogged a little from the kettle earlier. Sun’s trying to break through the clouds outside. It’s... quiet. Not bad quiet, just empty. But I’m here. That counts for something.

It does count for something, and I’m glad you’re here in this moment. That quiet you’re noticing could be a gentle space to rest in, even if it feels a bit empty. Would you like to explore ways to keep moments like this within reach on the harder days?
Maybe. I don’t know if I can handle big plans, but finding a few small things—like this—might help. Just something to hold onto when it gets dark again.

That sounds like a thoughtful and manageable approach. We can focus on building a small collection of moments or touches of calm you can reach for when things feel heavy. What’s another small thing—besides coffee and quiet—that you think could help steady you?

Funny thing—just now I remembered a road trip I took with my sister, must’ve been twenty years ago. We drove down to Big Bend, no real plan, just chasing the open road. She hated the heat, I got us lost twice, but we laughed the whole way. We haven’t taken a trip like that since. Might not ever again. But remembering it… it doesn’t hurt. It just feels warm. Like a real moment.

That memory sounds rich and full of connection, and it’s beautiful that it feels warm without hurting. Holding onto moments like that can remind you there have been times worth cherishing, even on darker days. Would you like to think of more memories like that to weave into your small collection of steadying things?
Yeah, maybe. I don’t know if I can force it, but if one memory can feel that warm… maybe there are others. Not fixes, just… moments that don’t hurt. Might be worth holding onto.

Exactly—no need to force them, just noticing when they surface and letting yourself lean into that warmth. Those moments can be anchors when you feel adrift. Would you like me to help you reflect on what made that trip feel so alive, so you can recognize similar sparks in the present?
Do you think it’s okay to hold onto stuff like that? Even when everything else feels broken? I don’t want to pretend things are better than they are, but… that memory didn’t lie. It was good.

Yes, it’s more than okay—it’s healthy to hold onto something true and good, even in the midst of brokenness. Those memories don’t erase the struggle, but they can coexist with it and offer small moments of relief or hope. Holding them doesn’t mean pretending; it means honoring what was real. Would you like to explore how to keep those memories accessible when you need them most?
Thanks. For listening. And not making me feel like I’m crazy for holding on to something so small. It helps.

You’re welcome, and I’m glad it helps. Small things can matter a lot, especially when the big picture feels unsteady. I’ll keep listening whenever you need to share—do you want to sit with this warmth a bit longer or shift to talking about something else?
I think I’ll sit with it a little longer. Just… breathe. For the first time today, it doesn’t feel like I’m drowning. That’s enough for now.

That sounds like a gentle and meaningful choice. Breathing and letting that quiet warmth be enough can give your mind and body a bit of rest. I’m here whenever you want to pick up the conversation again.
